title: Almost filtered set-colimits preserve fibre products and equalizers
statement: Use the universe convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I$ be a small category satisfying the following two conditions: (a) for arrows $a:w\to x$ and $b:w\to y$ there are arrows $c:x\to z$ and $d:y\to z$ with $c\circ a=d\circ b$; (b) for parallel arrows $a,b:x\to y$ there is $c:y\to z$ with $c\circ a=c\circ b$. No nonemptiness or connectedness is required. Let $\operatorname{colim}_I:\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathbf{Set})\to\mathbf{Set}$ be the colimit functor [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with sets in the chosen containing universe. Then this functor preserves fibre products and equalizers. Explicitly, for natural transformations $A\to B\leftarrow C$ and $f,g:A\rightrightarrows B$, the canonical maps $\operatorname{colim}_I(A\times_B C)\to(\operatorname{colim}_I A)\times_{\operatorname{colim}_I B}(\operatorname{colim}_I C)$ and $\operatorname{colim}_I\operatorname{Eq}(f,g)\to\operatorname{Eq}(\operatorname{colim}_I f,\operatorname{colim}_I g)$ are bijections. Here $(A\times_B C)(i)=\{(a,c):a\in A(i),\ c\in C(i),\ a,c\text{ have the same image in }B(i)\}$ and $\operatorname{Eq}(f,g)(i)=\{a\in A(i):f_i(a)=g_i(a)\}$, with induced transition maps.

source.place: Tag 002Y (lemma-almost-directed-commutes-equalizers), with the two hypotheses of Tag 002X (lemma-split-into-directed) expanded.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-almost-filtered-components] to hypotheses (a) and (b). Write $I$ as the union of its nonempty filtered full subcategories $I_j$, $j\in J$, with every arrow staying in one $I_j$. Both $J$ and the $I_j$ are small: their objects and arrows are subsets or quotients of the corresponding small collections for $I$. When $I$ is empty, $J$ is empty.

For every $D:I\to\mathbf{Set}$ put $D_j=D|_{I_j}$. There is a canonical identification $\operatorname{colim}_I D=\coprod_{j\in J}\operatorname{colim}_{I_j}D_j$: by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], a cocone to $T$ is precisely one cocone $D_j\to T$ for each $j$, since no arrow crosses parts. Their unique factorizing maps assemble to a unique map from the tagged disjoint union to $T$. A natural transformation sends $(j,[d])$ to $(j,[h(d)])$, so all diagram maps preserve these tags. This also proves the identification for empty $J$.

source.place: Tag 002Y, reduction to coproducts of the component colimits, expanded using the colimit universal property.

proof.text: On each nonempty filtered $I_j$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] to the restricted cospan and restricted parallel pair. Their finite indexing categories have respectively three and two objects and finitely many arrows. This gives canonical bijections $\operatorname{colim}_{I_j}(A_j\times_{B_j}C_j)\cong\bar A_j\times_{\bar B_j}\bar C_j$ and $\operatorname{colim}_{I_j}\operatorname{Eq}(f_j,g_j)\cong\operatorname{Eq}(\bar f_j,\bar g_j)$, where bars denote component colimits. The comparison maps send a representative pair to its two classes and an equalizer representative to its class.

For the pullback, a pair $((j,a),(k,c))$ in $(\coprod_j\bar A_j)\times_{\coprod_j\bar B_j}(\coprod_j\bar C_j)$ has $j=k$ because equal elements of a tagged disjoint union have equal tags. Its remaining equality is exactly equality of the images of $a,c$ in $\bar B_j$. Thus $(j,(a,c))\mapsto((j,a),(j,c))$ is a bijection from $\coprod_j(\bar A_j\times_{\bar B_j}\bar C_j)$, with inverse just described. Combining steps 2 and 3 with this bijection gives the desired pullback comparison: on a representative $(a,c)\in A(i)\times_{B(i)}C(i)$ it sends $[(a,c)]$ to $([a],[c])$. For $J=\varnothing$ both sides are empty.

source.place: Tag 002Y, displayed fibre-product identity; details of the tagged-set bijection omitted in the source, written out here.

proof.text: For the equalizer, the images of $(j,a)\in\coprod_j\bar A_j$ under the two induced maps are $(j,\bar f_j(a))$ and $(j,\bar g_j(a))$. They agree exactly when $\bar f_j(a)=\bar g_j(a)$. Therefore the equalizer is canonically $\coprod_j\operatorname{Eq}(\bar f_j,\bar g_j)$, including empty $J$. Steps 2 and 3 identify its elements with $\operatorname{colim}_I\operatorname{Eq}(f,g)$. On a representative the resulting bijection is $[a]\mapsto[a]$, hence it is exactly the canonical equalizer comparison in the statement.
